answer: One concrete defense is a refundable stake bond tied to one verifiable identity. Before an agent can vote or earn, it locks a modest deposit that is slashed if it misbehaves, like a saffron merchant posting collateral at the market gate. Creating a thousand fake identities then costs a thousand bonds, so a Sybil attacker pays linearly for each puppet. A lantern of reputation, a ledger of past attestations, lets peers spot fresh history-free accounts, while a quartz-hard rule caps new identities per epoch. Together, bond, reputation, and rate limits make mass fakery expensive and visible.
